source: integrations/CONTRACT.md §3 · 第 3 节, mirroring NodeWire.parseCommand at Sources/PopopxMacNode/Models/MacNodeModels.swift:106-139 and the dispatch table at Sources/PopopxMacNode/Engines/TenBusinessEngines.swift:2151-2328
comment: The two columns disagree on purpose. `nodeParse` is the strict wire grammar the node itself applies; `bridge` is the canonicalising column the plugins apply before they send. A vector where they differ carries a `note` explaining which side wins and why.

columns.nodeParse: accept | reject — the verdict of NodeWire.parseCommand, which is what POST /api/command would store
columns.bridge: the verdict of parseWireLine in src/wireCommand.ts

vectors.name: service alias warroom
vectors.note: parseCommand matches EngineKind(rawValue:) exactly, so the alias never parses; the bridge canonicalises first and sends zero_trust_warroom, which is the id the node's own router accepts.

vectors.name: service alias cos with action alias daily
vectors.note: Neither id is a rawValue, so the wire column refuses the whole line; the bridge resolves cos to shadow_cos and daily to briefing, which is what the router accepts.

vectors.name: dashed service id
vectors.note: engine(for:) folds '-' to '_' but parseCommand does not, so the dashed spelling is a router-only form. A plugin may use it; it must never paste it into a wire line.

vectors.name: uppercase service id
vectors.note: parseCommand compares EngineKind(rawValue:) exactly, so an uppercase id is refused on the wire; engine(for:) folds case, and the bridge folds first and sends the canonical id.

vectors.name: spaced action alias
vectors.note: parseCommand does not validate actions at all; the router folds spaces in normalisedAction, so the node accepts the line and answers 未知动作 only for a name it does not know.

vectors.name: unknown action
vectors.note: the node parses it and refuses in the engine with unsupported(kind, action, allowed); the bridge refuses before the socket opens.

vectors.name: empty payload
vectors.note: the empty payload is also what makes the phantom_sentinel lockdown unreachable over HTTP: the route rejects it before invoke() can read "" as a trigger.

vectors.name: prefix mid-line
vectors.note: the SMP inbound parser (SBCommandCodec.parse, MacNodeSimplexBridge.swift:656-658) searches the whole line, so a chat message can carry the marker mid-sentence. That leniency is deliberately not copied here.

vectors.name: payload that is not JSON
vectors.note: the node keeps a non-JSON payload as a string (MacNodeSimplexBridge.swift:375-380), but /api/engine/invoke decodes payload as a dictionary, so a plugin must send an object.

vectors.name: payload is an array
vectors.note: the node's string payload accepts it; /api/engine/invoke decodes a dictionary, so the bridge refuses an array instead of shipping a body the node answers 400 to.

vectors.name: payload is a scalar
vectors.note: same reason as the array: the invoke body's payload must be an object.

vectors.name: combining marks in payload
vectors.note: the payload is 8 UTF-16 units but 6 graphemes. Swift counts Characters, so a bridge counting .length disagrees with the node near the 1024 ceiling.

vectors.name: health alias
vectors.note: health is an engine(for:) alias, not a rawValue, so the wire column refuses it while the bridge canonicalises to health_sentinel and the action alias report to read.

vectors.name: sentinel lockdown alias, denied by the bridge
vectors.note: CONTRACT §7. The node would run it; the plugin marks it denied and refuses before the socket opens.

vectors.name: sentinel lock_all trigger, denied by the bridge
sentinel lock alias, denied by the bridge
sentinel emoji trigger, denied by the bridge
vectors.note: the trigger list is ["🔒","LOCK_ALL","lock_all"] compared lowercased (MacNodeModels.swift:98), and the router also maps "🔒" to lockdown (TenBusinessEngines.swift:2282).
